And with the worst drought in 1,500 years parching the region, water anxiety is increasing.

1.abstract: A recent report finds that home prices rose 14 percent nationally over a year. But not all markets are created equal.

8.abstract: Toyota Motor said on Friday that it will make about 40 percent fewer cars and trucks around the world in October as a result of complications from a shortage of computer chips and Covid-19 restrictions affecting the production of parts in Southeast Asia.

8.headline: Always Pay the Rent? It May Help Your Mortgage Application.
8.abstract: For decades, regular payments to a landlord haven’t counted for much for many tenants trying to get a mortgage. Fannie Mae aims to change that.

8.headline: There’s Amazon Prime, and Then There’s Shipping by Schooner
8.abstract: Against the winds of instantaneous everything, a sailboat crew tries to forge a carbon-neutral supply chain between the Hudson Valley and New York City.

9.headline: 800,000 New Yorkers Just Lost Federal Unemployment Benefits
9.abstract: Many pandemic-era federal programs expired on Sunday, leaving jobless New Yorkers with more modest state unemployment benefits, or no aid at all.

9.headline: Biden’s New Vaccine Push Is a Fight for the U.S. Economy
9.abstract: The effort reflects the continuing and evolving threat the coronavirus pandemic poses to the economic recovery.

9.headline: Newsom Beat the Recall, Now Comes the Hard Part: Governing California
9.abstract: Gov. Gavin Newsom is facing multiple crises. Ninety percent of California is in extreme drought. The median home price has eclipsed $800,000. Some 100,000 people are sleeping outside or in their cars.

9.headline: As Russians Vote, Resignation, Anger and Fear of a Post-Putin Unknown
9.abstract: Many in Russia say they are fed up with corruption, stagnant wages and rising prices. But they worry, as one man said, that “if things start to change, there will be blood.”

9.headline: Biden’s Entire Presidential Agenda Rests on Expansive Spending Bill
9.abstract: A plan for the economy, education, immigration, climate and more binds disparate Democratic lawmakers, but the proposal risks sinking under its own weight.

9.headline: Global Markets Swoon as Worries Mount Over Superpowers’ Plans
9.abstract: The S&P 500 closed down 1.7 percent over a number of jitters, like China’s sputtering real estate market and the phasing out of stimulus measures in the United States.

9.headline: Federal Reserve Signals a Shift Away From Pandemic Support
9.abstract: The Fed said it could soon slow its large-scale purchases of government-backed bonds and indicated it might raise interest rates in 2022.

9.headline: Thousands of N.Y. Health Care Workers Get Vaccinated Ahead of Deadline
9.abstract: Though many hospital and nursing home employees remain unvaccinated, officials say worst-case staffing shortages seem less likely.

9.headline: Yellen Warns of ‘Catastrophic’ Consequences From Debt Limit Breach
9.abstract: The Treasury secretary, testifying alongside Jerome H. Powell, the Federal Reserve chair, implored Congress to raise or suspend the nation’s borrowing cap before an Oct. 18 deadline.

9.headline: Gas Shortages Awaken Britain to Some Crucial Workers: Truck Drivers
9.abstract: Dwindling pay, poor roadside conditions and post-Brexit immigration rules have led to a critical shortage of drivers. Despite appeals, some say they are reluctant to return.

9.headline: Democrats Move to Avert Shutdown, but Divisions Imperil Biden’s Agenda
9.abstract: Democrats prepared a spending bill to keep the government funded past a Thursday deadline, but moderates dug in harder against their ambitious social safety net bill.

9.headline: House Delays Vote on Infrastructure Bill as Democrats Feud
9.abstract: A liberal revolt left Democrats short of votes, but leaders insisted they would bring up the measure again on Friday, giving them more time to reach a deal on a separate climate and safety net bill.

9.headline: ‘Everything Going the Wrong Way’: Dollar Stores Hit a Pandemic Downturn
9.abstract: Their business model is being tested by worker burnout, pressure to raise wages, supply chain problems and growing local opposition.

9.headline: Inflation Warning Signs Flash Red, Posing Challenge for Washington
9.abstract: Inflation, once expected to fade quickly, is proving more stubborn. That ramps up tension among officials as they wait for pressures to fade.

9.headline: Biden Pulls Back on Infrastructure Bill, Tying It to Social Policy Measure
9.abstract: After pressing toward a vote, Democratic leaders accepted “reality” that the bill could not pass before a broad climate change and safety net measure comes together.

9.headline: U.S. Signals No Thaw in Trade Relations With China
9.abstract: The Biden administration said it would not immediately remove the Trump administration’s tariffs and would require that Beijing uphold its trade commitments.

9.headline: Energy Prices Spike as Producers Worry Over Pandemic and Climate
9.abstract: Even as more costly fuel poses political risks for President Biden, oil companies and OPEC are not eager to produce more because they worry prices will drop.

9.headline: The Stock Market’s Hot Summer Became a Swoon. Where Does It Go Next?
9.abstract: Inflation and supply chain problems have been a concern since the pandemic began. But action by the Federal Reserve and pressure on corporate profits put those worries in sharp focus.

9.headline: ‘The Beginning of the Snowball’: Supply-Chain Snarls Delay Books
9.abstract: Shipping delays, printer backups and worker shortages are forcing publishers to postpone new titles and leaving booksellers in a lurch for some old ones.

9.headline: Stocks drop again as Big Tech tumbles.
9.abstract: Oil prices rose as OPEC met.

9.headline: How Other Nations Pay for Child Care. The U.S. Is an Outlier.
9.abstract: Rich countries contribute an average of $14,000 per year for a toddler’s care, compared with $500 in the U.S. The Democrats’ spending bill tries to shrink the gap.

9.headline: How a Vaccine Mandate Could Worsen a Shortage of Home Care Aides
9.abstract: Some 250,000 home health care workers must get the coronavirus vaccine by Friday, but tens of thousands of them have yet to receive it.

9.headline: Dealers pay record prices for used cars, reversing a trend that pointed to an easing of inflation.
9.abstract: Used car prices, normally a tiny contributor to overall inflation, have become a key influence on the direction of measures like the Consumer Price Index.

9.headline: Jobs Report Offers Little Reassurance on U.S. Economy
9.abstract: The gain of 194,000 in September showed the continuing grip of the latest coronavirus wave, though unemployment fell to 4.8 percent.

9.headline: When Child Care Costs Twice as Much as the Mortgage
9.abstract: President Biden’s social policy legislation aims to address a problem that weighs on many families — and the teachers and child care centers serving them.

9.headline: ‘It’s Not Sustainable’: What America’s Port Crisis Looks Like Up Close
9.abstract: An enduring traffic jam at the Port of Savannah reveals why the chaos in global shipping is likely to persist.

9.headline: World’s Growth Cools and the Rich-Poor Divide Widens
9.abstract: The International Monetary Fund says the persistence of the coronavirus and global supply chain crisis weighs on economies.

9.headline: Consumer Prices Jump Again, Presenting a Dilemma for Washington
9.abstract: Consumer Price Index data from the Labor Department showed that prices kept climbing in September, as supply chain snarls and rising rents fueled rapid inflation.

9.headline: The Fed prepared to slow support for the economy and worried about supply chain disruption at its last meeting.
9.abstract: Federal Reserve officials are preparing to slow bond buying and are divided over when they might need to raise interest rates as inflation bites.

9.headline: Biden Announces Measures at Major Ports to Battle Supply Chain Woes
9.abstract: The Port of Los Angeles will join the Port of Long Beach in operating 24/7 as the administration struggles to address a problem that is boosting inflation.

Schools were reopening, freeing up many caregivers. Surely, economists and business owners reasoned, a flood of workers would follow.

10.abstract: Supply chain disruptions, a worker shortage and pain at the gasoline pump have made inflation an economic and political problem for the White House.

10.abstract: A country in crisis is facing a severe fuel shortage that is pushing it to the brink of collapse.

10.abstract: As paid family leave and other priorities were taken out of the president’s plan, the largest piece became a $555 billion plan to fight climate change.

10.abstract: Because so many jobs depend on automaking, the industry’s production problems are causing the pain to ripple.

10.abstract: The Federal Reserve is dealing with high inflation at a time when millions of workers remain on the job market’s sidelines. Wednesday’s announcement that it will slow bond purchases is a step toward more normal monetary policy.

10.abstract: Progressives who had threatened to sink the measure agreed to support it after extracting a promise from moderates that they would ultimately back the social safety net and climate bill.

10.headline: Wages are rising, but can they keep up with inflation?
10.abstract: In the tug of war between wage growth and rising prices, it is not yet clear who is winning. It could matter for the Federal Reserve.

10.headline: Americans Are Flush With Cash and Jobs. They Also Think the Economy Is Awful.
10.abstract: The psychological effects of inflation seem to have the upper hand.

10.abstract: Speaker Nancy Pelosi agreed to a deal proposed by the Congressional Black Caucus, mobilizing one faction of Democratic lawmakers to win over two others.

10.headline: Retailers Scramble to Attract Workers Ahead of the Holidays
10.abstract: Signing bonuses, higher wages, even college tuition. Companies are using perks to entice new employees in an industry that has been battered by the pandemic.

10.headline: The Biggest Kink in America’s Supply Chain: Not Enough Truckers
10.abstract: Long hours and uncomfortable working conditions are leading to a shortage of truck drivers, which has compounded shipping delays in the United States.

10.headline: Fastest Inflation in 31 Years Puts More Heat on Washington
